Proposed commercial highlights (high level):
- Commitment: 12 months, committed GPU-hours equivalent to 8 dedicated vGPUs (baseline throughput target).
- Pricing: 12-month list discount equivalent to ~18% off standard hosted rates when applied to committed volume; additional discretionary credit (see onboarding).
- Onboarding credit: $40k applied to first two invoices (to offset migration effort).
- Egress: 5 TB/month free egress (all regions), thereafter standard egress rates; option for negotiated cap/flat egress for an incremental fee.
- POC: 90-day sandbox on dedicated pool (no extra provisioning fees) to validate runtime compatibility and perf.

Next steps: can Karthik and Grace confirm implementation timeline and whether we should offer extra credits vs lowering list price? I'll loop them in. If this looks directionally good I can send a tightened SOW (attached draft SOW_Orion_Initial_Draft.docx) and a DocuSign link.

Diego / Karthik — quick technical read:

Summary verdict (short): we can deliver within their constraints, but there are operational caveats and a measurable egress exposure that should be reflected in pricing or mitigations. Details below and attached notes.

Compatibility / runtime:
- Orion's models (GNN + long-context transformers) run on our Dedicated runtime; we can avoid a 2x cost uplift by enabling dynamic KV sharding and sequence-length-aware batching. That requires a small runtime config tweak and a 2-week integration POC (environment + perf tuning).

Egress and networking:
- If Orion wants private VPC peering and a flat egress cap, cloud-provider egress fees still apply unless we place a proxy/gateway inside their VPC (adds infra & ops cost). My rough estimate (attached egress_estimate.xlsx): 5 TB/month free is safe; above that expect $0.09/GB on average across regions given their traffic profile. With caching and prefix/KV reuse, effective egress will likely be lower but we should not promise unlimited.

Concessions and alternatives I recommend:
- Offer: 5 TB/month free egress, then standard rates; include an optional flat egress package (e.g., $X/month for up to 20 TB) as an add-on.
- Technical concession: free 90-day dedicated sandbox + two SRE support hours/week during POC.
- Operational: 3-week POC to validate perf (+ 1 week for security sign-off and peering).

Attachments: runtime_compatibility_notes.pdf, egress_estimate.xlsx

If we want to match ByteServe's net economics exactly (20% + 3 months free), I'd swap $40k onboarding credit into a staged credit tied to milestones (POC success + GA). That protects margins while being competitive. Happy to chat and craft exact language for the SOW.

— Grace
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sanjay — thanks again for the patience. Per our internal review we've tightened the counter and attached the formal counteroffer and SOW (Redwood_Counteroffer_20260816.pdf, SOW_Orion_Initial_Draft.docx). Highlights: 

- Commercial: 12-month commit with an effective 19% list discount on committed volume.
- Onboarding: $40k staged credit — $20k applied at contract signing, $20k paid after successful POC and production smoke tests.
- POC: 90-day sandbox on dedicated pool (free), SRE support during POC (2 hrs/week).
- Egress: 5 TB/month free; above that standard egress rates apply. If Orion opts for a flat egress bucket (up to 20 TB/month) we can include that for an incremental monthly fee (TBD in SOW).
- Legal / timing: DocuSign packet is ready here: https://docusign.com/ORION-REDWOOD-2026. We need a signed contract by 2026-09-15 to secure the dedicated pool for Q4 onboarding.

Next steps:
1) Review attached counter + SOW and flag any redlines for legal.
2) If acceptable, sign DocuSign and we'll schedule the kickoff and POC within 7 business days of signature.

If you want a different split (e.g., deeper list discount instead of staged credit), we can consider a 20% list discount but would need to shorten the POC concession & limit SRE time to protect runway. Let me know which is preferable and we can adapt quickly.
